scope: CPU selector-matrix traffic and storage-layout experiments. Research controls only; no production cache or arithmetic changes.

fixture.matrix_layouts: Packed4-column8-term and wide8-column4-term fused component dots. Production has529 selector rows; the benchmark uses528 to exclude the scalar row remainder, a0.19% payload difference.
fixture.data: Deterministic public canonical residues; no encrypted keys or ciphertexts.

traffic_method: Same allocated selector dataset. Compare the full fused matrix, a256-point tiled read, and flat row reads. Every selector word contributes to an XOR oracle. Matrix outputs match their warm matrix reference byte for byte; proxies are validated against the complete scalar XOR, not against matrix outputs. Warm all methods; matrix/tiled/flat/flat/tiled/matrix,5 samples per block. Ten samples per method/layout. Buffers exceed CPU cache; no concurrent compilation or other benchmarks.
traffic_interpretation: For four columns, selector-only reads cost about30.2ms versus36.9ms for the full matrix. This points to limited headroom from dot/address arithmetic alone while retaining this data volume. These are logical bytes per second, not measured DRAM transactions. Proxy timings are not hardware lower bounds and exclude all public-table arithmetic/traffic; they cannot prove an irreducible machine gap or paper parity.
layout_method: Use the same matrix arithmetic and values with original vector rows, spans into those rows, contiguous per-prime4KiB-page slabs, transparent-large-page slabs, and both slab types with64-byte row padding. All mappings align to2MiB. Symmetric original/view/plain/huge/plain-padded/huge-padded/huge-padded/plain-padded/huge/plain/view/original sequence,5 repeats per block. All matrix outputs byte-identical. Advice occurs before first touch; setup/copying/page allocation excluded from timers.

initial_hint_only.interpretation: MADV_HUGEPAGE was accepted but /proc/self/smaps showed0 anonymous huge pages: this process inherited THP disabled. These timings do not establish large-page performance.

actual_large_page_configuration.scope: A guard temporarily enables THP in the benchmark process and restores its inherited process setting at scope exit. MADV_NOHUGEPAGE controls retain small pages. No machine-wide setting is changed.
actual_large_page_configuration.verification: Both layouts observe exactly the expected aggregate2MiB-page payload for17 unpadded33-page slabs and17 padded34-page slabs. The second layout again inherits THP disabled, verifying restoration after the first layout.

decision: Do not adopt any tested layout. Four-column original storage beats every slab variant; unpadded huge pages are substantially slower. Padding recovers most of the loss. Wide8-column padded layouts gain only about1–1.5%, while regressing four columns. Retain the existing cache.

retained_context.interpretation: Logical scan arithmetic and an Amdahl-style estimate holding all other stage costs fixed. This is not a hardware lower bound or an apples-to-apples paper comparison. Matrix-only tuning cannot supply a whole-bootstrap10x gain in this model.

limitations: One CPU, deterministic public fixtures and10 measured samples per method/layout. The528-row prototype is close to, but not identical to, the529-row retained matrix. Results do not justify modifying the production memory policy, declaring the remaining gap entirely hardware-related, or claiming a whole-FBS speedup.
